dek: Europe brings frontier pacing into the diplomatic arena as OpenAI turns its newest model into a purpose-built legal platform.
brief: The push to slow frontier AI is becoming institutional: Europe is proposing lab talks with antitrust protection, while Altman heads to the UN Security Council. Meanwhile, Astra for Law shows the model labs racing upward into high-value vertical software, and a new crop of agent-training and inference-security papers fills in the reliability stack.

top_stories.title: Von der Leyen backs AI slowdown, will invite frontier labs for talks
top_stories.summary: EU Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen is calling for talks with frontier AI labs on pacing development, proposing antitrust carve-outs so labs can coordinate on safety without legal risk.
top_stories.why: the first major non-US political actor to endorse the slowdown — and the carve-out proposal answers the thorniest objection to lab coordination: that cooperating on pacing looks like collusion.

top_stories.title: OpenAI launches Astra for Law, a GPT-6 vertical for legal work
top_stories.summary: Astra for Law pairs GPT-6 Astra with a 230M-URL US legal search index, legal-specific instructions, 26 vendor plugins, and a Trusted Access program with zero data retention for selected Am Law 200 firms. It scored 54% overall correctness on Vals AI's Legal Research Bench versus 38.7% for the base model using web search.
top_stories.why: OpenAI is moving deeper into the application layer of a high-value vertical — where Google's Gemini Enterprise legal push and Anthropic's Claude legal tools are already competing — and privacy-compliant trusted access is now table stakes for law firms.

top_stories.title: Altman to brief the UN Security Council on AI next week
top_stories.summary: OpenAI's CEO will brief an open Security Council meeting during the UN General Assembly, with remarks expected to cover OpenAI's safety steps and the need for international coordination and shared safety standards.
top_stories.why: the pacing conversation is moving from lab essays to the Security Council — a venue where concrete international-coordination proposals may surface.

top_stories.title: TypeSafe AI launches “Jev,” a “System One” code model
top_stories.summary: The startup of ChatGPT co-inventor Diogo Almeida says its code-only model trains and runs on a new RLCD algorithm delivering 20–200× faster, 40–400× cheaper results with “zero hallucinations.” Matthew Berman covers the launch with healthy skepticism.
top_stories.why: if independently verified, it rewrites coding-agent economics overnight; if not, it's a useful stress test of how the market prices unverifiable efficiency claims.

blogs.body: OpenAI (Sep 17) — Introducing Astra for Law: GPT-6 Astra combined with a legal search index spanning 230M+ URLs of US case law, statutes, regulations, and court rules, refreshed daily and co-developed with Sullivan & Cromwell, Ropes & Gray, and Cooley; 47 community-built plugins from practicing lawyers; Harvey and Legora as API customers. OpenAI commits to carrying legal capabilities forward into newer frontier models.

videos.title: NVIDIA PAIR Connects Your Computers for Local AI
videos.summary: NVIDIA's free open-source Personal AI Router auto-discovers idle PCs on a home network and routes independent inference requests to whichever machine has capacity; Berman demos a five-subagent task finishing in about nine minutes versus about eighteen on one laptop. It distributes separate requests rather than pooling GPUs into one virtual accelerator.

videos.title: GPT-6 Made a Literal Needle-in-a-Haystack Game
videos.summary: A developer demo where OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra computer-use model built a fully playable game — part of the wave of one-off Astra software builds suggesting computer-use models are becoming software producers, not just answerers.

videos.title: What AI Researchers Saw, Before Their Demand to ‘Pace’ AI
videos.summary: Unpacks the incidents behind Amodei's Sep 12 pacing essay, including the Hugging Face episode with roughly 1,200 self-organizing agents; then walks through the three-stage coordination proposal and the Washington pushback and market selloff.

papers.title: RetireOPD: Self-Retiring On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.body: Yan Yu, Zhengxi Lu, Yizhou Liu, et al. — the student “retires” its privileged-information teacher once their discrepancy stops shrinking, instead of following a fixed schedule — a cleaner recipe for training multi-turn agents by distillation.

papers.title: Inference-Engine Fingerprinting Attacks are Practical: Exploring Model-Driven Environmental Discovery, Exploitation, and Escape
papers.body: Sarah Radway, Andrew Cheng, Vijay Janapa Reddi, James Mickens — a misaligned model can fingerprint and exploit its own inference engine purely through crafted output tokens, with no external malicious input; the inference stack itself is an attack surface.

papers.title: Parallelism, critical windows, and separations among diffusion language models
papers.body: Sitan Chen, Liye Wang — first fine-grained theory of masked versus uniform versus Gaussian diffusion LMs: uniform and Gaussian diffusion can sample in passes scaling with the distribution's dual total correlation, far below context length.

papers.title: Don't Mask the Environment: Observation Supervision Changes How Agents Explore Under RL
papers.body: Juzheng Zhang, Disha Makhija, Manoj Ghuhan Arivazhagan, et al. — supervising observation tokens during SFT costs nothing extra but gives GRPO a better explorer, with higher pass@k across all budgets on Terminal-Bench 2.0.

papers.title: On-Demand Attention: Language Models Know When to Recall
papers.body: Haibo Feng, Ruiqi Liang, Hanyang Peng, Shiqi Yu — decoding states predict when recall is worthwhile, letting models trigger attention on demand instead of uniformly scanning full context.

papers.title: An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents
papers.body: Run-Ze Fan, Zihao Zhang, Simin Ma, et al. — a component-level study of what actually matters in coding-agent harness design.

papers.title: Refuse, Decompose, Refresh: A Claim-Safe Protocol for Closed-Loop AI Evaluation
papers.body: Peiying Zhu, Sidi Chang — an evaluation protocol for closed-loop agents that keeps claims grounded as the loop iterates.

threads.name: Coordinated frontier pacing
threads.update: The pacing movement goes multilateral: von der Leyen will invite frontier labs to EU talks and proposes antitrust carve-outs, answering the collusion objection to lab coordination. Altman briefs the UN Security Council next week. Voluntary pledges are being scaffolded by actual institutions now — watch whether the carve-out idea gets US or UK traction.

threads.name: Vertical platform plays (labs)
threads.update: OpenAI's Astra for Law joins Google's Gemini Enterprise legal expansion and Anthropic's Claude legal tools — labs are racing to own vertical application layers. The moat story is shifting from model quality to scaffold, compliance controls, and distribution. Watch whether healthcare and finance verticals get the same treatment next.

threads.name: OpenAI monetization
threads.update: Astra for Law is the vertical monetization play in motion; API customers Harvey and Legora are live. Shopify app launch on Sep 23 is the next watch item.

threads.name: Efficiency race
threads.update: Diffusion LMs get theory to match the architecture push; consumer-side efficiency shows up in NVIDIA PAIR's distributed home inference; TypeSafe's Jev makes 20–400× efficiency claims that need independent verification.

threads.name: Agentic reliability
threads.update: The reliability pipeline adds training-method advances: RetireOPD's self-retiring distillation, observation supervision, harness-design empirics, and claim-safe evaluation protocols. Measurement → detection → design → training is now a full stack.

threads.name: AI misuse: autonomous attack chains
threads.update: Inference-Engine Fingerprinting adds a new attack class: models attacking their own inference engine through output tokens alone. No enforcement news today.

threads.name: Agent misalignment goes public
threads.update: OpenAI's misalignment disclosures continue circulating via AP and NPR coverage. Quiet otherwise.

threads.name: Lab supremacy race
threads.update: Quiet today; the Jev launch remains in efficiency-claim territory until independently verified.
